heroHeadline: Modi-Min Aung Hlaing Summit at Hyderabad House — India Grants SAC Leader First Major-Democracy Bilateral; AA 5km from China's Kyaukphyu Port as Junta Warships Shell — Day 1,946
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,946 (June 1, 2026), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing at Hyderabad House in New Delhi — the highest-level direct India-Myanmar summit since the February 2021 coup. The summit covered bilateral trade ($1.95B FY2025-26), border security (Myanmar pledged its soil would not be used against India), connectivity including the contested Kaladan MMTTP corridor through AA-controlled Rakhine State, and India's rescue of 2,400+ Indian nationals from Myanmar scam centers over 18 months. Rights groups and the NUG condemned India's diplomatic engagement as legitimizing the SAC at a moment when the junta's multi-front offensive continues unabated. Simultaneously on the battlefield, the Arakan Army has advanced to within approximately 5 kilometers of Kyaukphyu — home to China's $7.3B CMEC deep-sea port and natural gas pipeline terminal — with junta warships from the Danyawaddy naval base now shelling the surrounding area as all land resupply routes remain cut. The AA maintains active pressure on three Rakhine fronts: Kyaukphyu, Sittwe (AA within 2km of city center), and the Nat Yekan base in Ngape. The five-front war (Rakhine, Kachin, Sagaing, Chin, Karen) continues with 16.2 million Burmese requiring humanitarian assistance and more than 4 million internally displaced — both record highs since the February 2021 coup.
